h: Rivers, Reservoirs and Rochdale's Own Gracie
p: Riverside is part of a big transformation of Rochdale town centre, and the area around it has changed a lot in recent years. One of the most striking projects was the reopening of the River Roch through the town centre. For decades the river was covered over, but it was uncovered again, revealing a historic bridge that had been hidden for years. It's well worth a look before or after your round.

Rochdale is also the hometown of Gracie Fields, the much-loved singer and actress who was a household name across Britain in the 1930s. A statue of her stands outside the Town Hall, so make sure to give her a wave. It's a fun fact to share with the kids, and a reminder of the town's proud history.

For anyone who fancies some fresh air after a round of golf, the countryside around Rochdale is beautiful. Hollingworth Lake Country Park, near Littleborough, is a large reservoir surrounded by walking paths, with a visitor centre, cafés and boats to hire in season. It's a lovely spot for a walk or a picnic with stunning views of the Pennine hills.

Healey Dell Nature Reserve, on the northern edge of town, is a hidden gem, with woodland trails, waterfalls and a dramatic old railway viaduct crossing the gorge. It's a great place to explore with kids, especially if they like a bit of adventure.

If you're planning to visit Putt & Play with younger children, it's worth thinking about when to go. Weekends and school holidays are busy, so a weekday afternoon might give you a quieter round. With so much to explore in and around Rochdale, it's easy to turn a game of mini golf into a full day out.
